title: feat(002, 003, 004, 006): the availability matrix, corpus-true chips, spec-spine-first adoption, and 006's errata
body:
## Summary

Publishes the three copy tiers the owner chose on 2026-09-12 (revision-4 row WEB-01), reconciled with the answers adopted the same day, and records spec 006's errata after its approval flip (WEB-04).

**Stacked on #12.** The base is #12's branch so the diff is only this change. Merge #12 first; this PR then retargets to `main` and is rebased to drop the duplicate flip. Merging to `main` deploys the apex.

- **The availability matrix** (spec 004 section 3.3.1): `/products` opens with capabilities read as implemented, released, exercised and hosted. Implemented is rolled up from the baked registry; the other axes are authored with public evidence, and the loader fails the prerender on any row rule.
- **Chips report the corpus** (spec 002 section 9): implemented, in progress, pending, on the ladder, the loop, the for-agents block and the docs stubs, each linking the matrix for the other axes.
- **spec-spine first** (spec 004 section 3.5): `/get-started` leads with governing a repository you already have. The local engine reads not released until a release containing it has been tested on a clean machine, and `install.sh` is described only as the v0.1.0 CLI and MCP server install.
- **Corrections**: attest-ledger signs its genesis anchor against the key the anchor carries; statecrafting's MPL-2.0 packages; "self-hostable"; a stale repo count; spec-spine 085 implemented and unreleased.
- **Public evidence only** (WEB-03): publishing drafts is not authorized, so nothing published rests on statecraft spec 014, which is on no public branch. The docs self-host stub, the whitepaper's ledger and verifier paragraphs, figure 2, spec 002 section 8, spec 004 section 8 and spec 006 sections 1 and 3 now cite statecraft 008 and 009 or say "no public record".
- **Spec 006 section 10**: the adopted decisions restated in full, six errata, and the table of re-pointed evidence.

Not in this PR: thesis-dependent copy (the hero, rahi, the superseded whitepaper), which is a separate follow-on that cannot build until statecraft publishes 014; and the `app/` ownership narrowing, which is #13 and merges in either order.

## Testing

On spec-spine 0.18.0 against `origin/main` `f074586`:

- `spec-spine compile`, `index`, `lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0), `check` (both trees fresh), `couple --base origin/main` (17 paths, no drift, no waiver), `index coverage --fail-on-untraced` (33/33); `make typecheck build` exit 0, 147 prerendered pages.
- Built HTML: "Ed25519-signed", "can sign entries", "self-hostable", "Ten open repos", "unsigned today", "never run in production" on 0 pages; "MPL-2.0" and "genesis anchor" on 146; no off-origin `script`, `link`, `img`, `iframe` or `source`.
- Every external evidence URL in the matrix resolved (crates.io and npm checked through their APIs).
- Matrix negative tests, each reverted, positive control rebuilt after: an unresolved registry id, hosted yes on a partial row, a yes reading with no evidence (tsc and build), a non-public host, an unpublished statecraft draft as evidence, a repo off the roster, a read-at of `main`. All refused with exit 1 (tsc 2).
- Merged locally with the ownership PR's branch: clean merge, gate and build exit 0.
- Visual review from headless Chrome captures at 1280px of `/products`, `/get-started`, `/` and the self-host stub. The 390px capture clips on the right exactly as unchanged `main` does, so mobile is not verified by this run.
- Specs 002, 003, 004 and 006 declare no `verify:cli` block, so `spec-spine verify` reports not-declared for them and was not used as evidence.

title: refactor(001, 005): claim app/ files by name, and record what coupling does not prove
body:
## Summary

Narrows spec 001's blanket `app/` claim, separately from any copy change, on the owner's 2026-09-12 adoption of revision-4 row WEB-05 (spec 006 D-10). Independent of #12 and of the publication PR; merge in either order.

- **Spec 001** claims the ten files under `app/` its section 3 defines, by name, instead of the directory. Every other `app/` file is already claimed by name by spec 002, 003 or 004, so coverage stays total and spec 004's `extends` edges still resolve. Section 7 records the decision.
- **Spec 005 section 8** records what the ratchet does now under `app/`, and the finding WEB-05 asks to report: a comment appended to an owning spec satisfies the coupling gate. Coupling presence is not proof of substantive specification review. Three requests to spec-spine are recorded there, and no copy change waits on them.

## Testing

On spec-spine 0.18.0, probes in throwaway worktrees with a probe commit on the named revision, `couple --base origin/main`:

| Probe | `main` at `f074586` | this change |
|---|---|---|
| unclaimed `app/lib/unclaimed-claim.ts`, `index coverage --fail-on-untraced` | exit 0, 33/33 | exit 1, 32/33 |
| the same file, `couple` | exit 1, C-001 owner 001 | exit 1, C-002 |
| a line in `app/lib/products.ts`, no spec edit | exit 1, C-001 owners 001 and 004 | exit 1, C-001 owner 004 |
| the same line plus a comment in spec 001 | exit 0 | exit 1 |
| the same line plus a comment in spec 004 | exit 0 | exit 0 |

- `spec-spine compile`, `index`, `lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0), `check` (fresh; 31 unwitnessed claims, all allowed, where main reports 23), `couple --base origin/main` (no drift), `index coverage --fail-on-untraced` (32/32); `make typecheck build` exit 0.
- `spec-spine verify 005-governed-agentic-loop`: passed, 15 commands. Spec 001 declares no `verify:cli` block, so its verify reports not-declared.
- Merged locally with the publication PR's branch: clean merge, 33/33 claimed, gate and build exit 0, and the unclaimed-file probe refused as C-002.

title: docs(006): ratify the claim inventory on the owner's approval
body:
Flips `006-claim-inventory-and-realignment` from `draft` to `approved`, on the
owner's explicit approval, and commits the two regenerated shards with it.

## What this ratifies

The record now carries the corpus's authority:

- section 3, the claim inventory: every claim the site publishes, classified as
  verified available, current implementation work, proposed, historical or
  unsupported, with the evidence named
- section 4, the proposals
- section 5, the requests to sibling repositories
- section 6, the vocabulary packet for `statecrafting-profile`

## What this does not do

Nothing becomes schedulable. The spec keeps `implementation: n-a` because it is
a record, not a work order, and `spec-spine registry plan` still reports 0 ready
and 0 blocked.

Section 8 is unchanged and still authorizes no publication: no copy change
beyond the corrections that landed under specs 002, 003 and 004 in #11, and no
deploy. Specs 002, 003 and 004 still require exactly what they required.

The five decisions in section 7 remain open and are the owner's to make:

| | Decision | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 | Is statecraft spec 014's successor thesis adopted? | P-2, P-3, P-5, P-7, and every "stamp" sentence on the site. Owned by the `statecraft` repo, not this one |
| D-2 | Availability matrix on `/products` or its own route? | P-1 |
| D-3 | Does the site name `rahi` before statecraft 017 has migrated anything? | the family roster |
| D-4 | Does the ladder gain the declared-against-exercised axis? | the ladder copy |
| D-5 | Is the whitepaper re-authored or superseded? | depends on D-1 |

## Verification

The spec's `## Verification` block, run verbatim. All six exit 0:

```
spec-spine compile                            exit 0
spec-spine index                              exit 0
spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn                exit 0
spec-spine check                              exit 0
spec-spine index coverage --fail-on-untraced  exit 0
make typecheck build                          exit 0
```

`spec-spine verify 006-claim-inventory-and-realignment` reports `not-declared`
(the block carries no `verify:cli` commands, so the verb skips it and exits 0
without running anything). The six commands were therefore run by hand; the
exit codes above are from those runs, not from the verb.

`make gate` is green against the committed change, with
`spec-spine couple: OK: 1 path(s) checked, no drift`. No waiver is needed.

Merging deploys to the live apex, so the merge stays a human checkpoint.

title: docs(006): the claim inventory, and the corrections that needed no decision
body:
## Summary

statecraft.ing's half of the 2026-09-11 family realignment. Spec 006 inventories
every claim this site publishes and classifies each one as verified available,
current implementation work, proposed, historical or unsupported, with the
evidence named and read at pinned sibling shas.

The corrections that needed no decision land with it:

- **The retired auth host.** The whitepaper and figure 3 said the OIDC signer
  was live at `auth.statecraft.ing`. That host is deliberately gone; rauthy runs
  inside the plane's own container, issuer `https://app.statecraft.ing/auth/v1/`
  (statecraft spec 009 section 2.4).
- **Static non-overlap stated as proof.** "Provably disjoint ... cannot collide"
  claimed more than the mechanism delivers. The copy now says what the coupling
  gate checks and what it does not cover: generated files, lockfiles, migrations,
  fixtures, and no OS-level write isolation.
- **A signed ledger that is not signed.** Ed25519 signing is a capability of the
  `attest-ledger` library, not a property of the record. The running plane's
  chain is hash-linked and unsigned (statecraft spec 014 section 3.5), so the
  copy separates integrity from issuer trust.
- **A verifier path nothing has exercised.** tenant-tail is described as a
  library shape; the factory has not stamped an application in production
  (014 section 3.3).
- **Three claims that fell behind the siblings.** The MCP face moves to present
  tense (statecraft-cli 105 is complete), the born-with certificate is recorded
  as built (enrahitu 012 complete, 009 still in progress), and the self-host stub
  tells both halves: the plane runs, and there is no reproducible install path.
- **One drift fix.** `papers.ts` read a hardcoded "10" for the family count,
  stale since the eleventh repo joined. It now reads `PRODUCT_FAMILY.length`.

Spec 006 is a record, not a work order: it amends no approved spec and authorizes
no publication. Everything that would change what spec 002 section 2 or spec 004
section 3.3 *require* is held back as proposals P-1 to P-7 for review, because
the successor thesis that would motivate them (statecraft spec 014) is still
`status: draft`. Specs 002, 003 and 004 gain dated status notes only.

## Testing

The gate as AGENTS.md lists it, every command exit 0:

- `spec-spine compile`, `spec-spine index`
- `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn`: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `spec-spine check`: spec-registry fresh, codebase-index fresh
- `spec-spine index coverage --fail-on-untraced`: 32/32 source files claimed
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD`: 11 paths, no drift
- `make typecheck build`

One honest note on acceptance: `spec-spine verify 006-claim-inventory-and-realignment`
exits 0 but runs nothing, reporting `not-declared (no verify:cli commands under
## Verification)` because the block is an untagged `sh` block. The six commands
in that block were run by hand instead, each exit 0.

title: fix(002, 004): re-point the ladder at the renumbered cli corpus, place the eleventh repo
body:
## Summary

Repairs the two build-time assertions that have kept `npm run build` red, and
with it the Pages deploy on `main`, since 2026-07-23. Both checks were correct;
neither had been answered.

**The ladder pointed at a corpus that renumbered itself.** `statecraft-cli`
merged the `claude-observatory` corpus into its own (its spec
`110-corpus-merge`) and moved its original specs into the `1xx` range. Four
references here stopped resolving: the three M5 rungs in
`app/lib/milestones.ts` and the for-agents `AGENT_REF` in
`app/routes/_index.tsx`. They are re-pointed at `101-cli-mcp-thesis`,
`104-governance-verbs` and `105-mcp-server`, which are the same three specs
under their post-merge ids, each `complete` in the baked payload. Nothing is
re-curated: `rollupMilestone` still reads live state from the shards, so the
position on the ladder stays a function of the sibling repos rather than a
claim this repo makes.

**The eleventh roster repo had no layer and no catalog entry.** Spec 003 added
`statecrafting` in #8; the products loader asserts that every roster repo sits
in exactly one `ARCHITECTURE_LAYERS` entry and has a `PRODUCT_DETAIL` record,
and it had neither. That assertion is what turned the deploy red on the very
commit that added it.

`statecrafting` goes in **Substrate**: it holds the `@statecrafting/*` napi
addons and the Encore build toolchain `enrahitu` vendors through its own
`008-vendored-encore-toolchain`, which is the layer `enrahitu` already
occupies. The layer blurb is extended so a layer listing two repos describes
both rather than only the chassis. The catalog entry makes three claims, each
checkable against the repo, including the license shape spec 003 section 3
already records (Apache-2.0 at the root, two packages AGPL-3.0).

## Spec coupling

Both owning specs carry a dated status note saying what moved and why: spec
002 section 7 for the ladder, spec 004 section 7 for the layer and the catalog.
No requirement changed. Spec 002 section 2 already told the implementing
session to check the registries for the then-current truth rather than trust a
sentence, and this is that instruction being followed rather than a design
being rewritten to fit code.

`spec-spine couple --base origin/main` reports 5 paths checked, no drift, no
waiver: each changed module travels with the spec that owns it.

## Testing

```
make gate            exit 0   check fresh, lint 0/0, coverage 32/32, couple 5 paths no drift
make typecheck       exit 0
make build           exit 0   every route prerendered
```

`make build` passing is the headline: it is the first green build since
2026-07-23. The `build` job that went red on #9 is the job that surfaced this,
and it should go green here.

title: feat(005): adopt the spec-spine 0.18.0 kit as this repository's harness
body:
Adopts the spec-spine 0.18.0 Claude Code kit as this repository's governed
agentic harness, and gives that harness an owning spec so the coupling gate
holds it.

## Why a spec for the harness

`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and all of `.claude/` sat outside the authority
graph. Spec 000 claims `spec-spine.toml` and the CI workflow; nothing claimed
the harness those two exist to defend, so an edit to the session hooks, the
permission allow-list or the backlog protocol was an ungoverned change to the
rules of governance itself. Spec 005 claims them, and `couple` now refuses a
change to `.claude/settings.json` that does not travel with a change to the
spec.

## What the kit brings

The harness here was frozen at spec-spine 0.10.0: five skills, three rules, an
init protocol predating `check`, `registry plan` and `verify`. The binary has
moved eight minor versions.

- **Ten skills**, byte-identical to the kit, sequencing the loop: `/prime`,
  `/setup`, `/next`, `/build`, `/verify`, `/ship`, `/shepherd`, `/spec`, plus
  the `/commit` and `/code-review` skills the loop calls. `/init` is gone;
  `/prime` replaces it and dispatches to `AGENTS.md`, so Codex CLI, Cursor and
  Copilot read the same steps. Keeping them byte-identical makes the next kit
  update a copy rather than a merge.
- **Four rules**, including `derived-artifacts-are-compiler-output.md` scoped
  to `.derived/**`.
- **Four agents** carrying this repo's site surface, the npm stack gate, and
  the content rules from spec 001 section 2 and spec 002 section 1.
- **Read-only hooks.** The `Stop` hook no longer regenerates the index: a
  session that has ended cannot commit the result, so it left `.derived/`
  dirty for whoever came next. `PreToolUse` now refuses a push that would
  update `main`, which deploys to the live apex.
- **`Makefile` and the merge driver.** `make gate` is the read-only chain,
  `make refresh` the writing half, `make typecheck build` the stack gate. CI
  runs the same targets, so the three callers cannot drift. `.githooks/` ships
  the shard merge driver, opt-in per clone.

## Three config defects the upgrade exposed

All silent until the binary got new enough to name them:

- **Five dead globs.** `standards/**`, `.github/workflows/**`,
  `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/rules/**` and `.claude/skills/**` matched
  directories only, never the files under them. None of those governance
  surfaces had ever contributed a byte to any content hash: the index was
  signing a ledger that had not read the harness. Now `L-010`.
- **A CI pin four minor versions behind.** The workflow installed `v0.10.0`
  to judge a corpus governed at 0.18.0. It now runs the `make gate` chain at
  the floor `[meta] required_version` declares, and its actions are SHA-pinned
  like `deploy.yml` (spec 001 section 2).
- **Generated output counted as source.** `.react-router/` typegen output put
  fourteen files in the unclaimed column, which made the ownership ratchet
  impossible to set honestly.

With those fixed, coverage is 32/32 and `[coupling] require_ownership` is on.
`lint --fail-on-warn` goes from 31 warnings to zero: the L-010 globs repaired,
and the 25 L-008 unwitnessed claims under `app/` declared in
`[lint] unwitnessed_allowed` rather than folded into every shard hash, which
would restale all seven shards on every routine page edit.

Both edits to spec 000's units are cleared by `extends` edges, not a waiver.
The bootstrap spec is untouched.

## Gate

```
spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn         0 errors, 0 warnings
spec-spine check                       both trees fresh
spec-spine index coverage              32/32 specifically claimed
spec-spine couple --base origin/main   30 paths checked, no drift
spec-spine verify 005                  passed (15 commands)
make gate                              exit 0
npm run typecheck                      exit 0
```

All four hooks were exercised directly: the push gate blocks `git push origin
main`, allows a feature branch, allows a tag push, and ignores a command that
merely mentions the verb.

## Known red: the build job, for reasons this PR did not cause

`npm run build` fails on two content drifts outside this spec's territory,
both pre-existing. `deploy.yml` on `main` has been red since 2026-07-23 for
the first of them:

1. `app/lib/products.ts`: `ARCHITECTURE_LAYERS` never placed `statecrafting`,
   the eleventh roster repo spec 003 added in #8.
2. `app/lib/milestones.ts` lines 112-114 cite `statecraft-cli` specs
   `001-cli-mcp-thesis`, `004-governance-verbs` and `005-mcp-server`, which
   that repo has since renumbered away; its corpus is now 71 specs starting
   `000-bootstrap`, `001-observed-universe`, `002-filesystem-watcher`.

Both are published-claim decisions under specs 002/003/004 and are fixed in a
follow-up change. The build job stays in this PR deliberately: it is what
surfaced a break that had been silently red for seven weeks.

title: feat(003): the statecrafting packages repo joins the product family
body:
First ordinary roster edit under spec 003: the shared native packages repo (the @statecrafting/* napi addons and the Encore toolchain) joins as the eleventh member, appended after trust-window in both the spec 003 section 3 table and app/lib/product-family.ts, so the footer, index family section, and repoMeta lookup pick it up.

The recompile also caught a stale derived artifact: the codebase-index by-package shard was still named stagecraft-ing.json from before the package rename; it is now statecrafting.json.

Gates: compile, index, lint --fail-on-warn, index check, and couple --base origin/main all green locally; no waiver needed (this is exactly the edit shape spec 003 exists for).

title: fix(004): point the sign-in link at the login initiator, not the proxy path
body:
## The bug

Clicking **Sign in** on https://statecraft.ing sends the user to
`https://app.statecraft.ing/auth/rauthy`, which returns a
`BadRequest` / "cross-origin request forbidden for this resource".

`/auth/rauthy` is the control plane's **rauthy proxy passthrough**, not a login
route. A top-level cross-site navigation to it is refused by rauthy's own CSRF
guard (`csrf_protection.rs`). Spec 004 §3.2 called it "the OIDC kickoff path the
app used before the apex cutover", which is not true of the live control plane.

## The fix

Point at `https://app.statecraft.ing/api/v1/auth/login`, the control plane's
**driver-agnostic login initiator**. It 302s to the active auth driver's OIDC
kickoff (rauthy today), so it also survives a driver change without another edit
here.

Verified live with browser-style headers (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`,
`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`):

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `/auth/rauthy` (old) | 400 cross-origin refusal |
| `/api/v1/auth/login` (new) | 302 to `/api/v1/auth/rauthy/login` then `/oidc/authorize?...scope=...groups...` |

Updates the component + comment and all four references in spec 004 (summary,
the §3.2 rationale with the correction recorded, and two acceptance/summary
lines).

## Also in this PR: a pre-existing derived refresh

`.derived` was **already stale on `main`**, independent of this change: PR #6
merged with its `govern` check red. The `by-package` shard was still named
`stagecraft-ing` while `package.json` is `statecrafting`, and the 001-003
registry shards had drifted. Regenerating under the CI-pinned spec-spine
`v0.10.0` (verified: `index check` fresh, `lint --fail-on-warn` clean, `couple`
no drift) brings the whole tree current, which is why shards for specs I did not
edit appear in the diff. This is what makes the governance gate green again.

Flagging it explicitly rather than folding it in silently: if you would rather
land the derived refresh separately, say so and I will split it.

title: feat(004): restore rich marketing surfaces (products, whitepaper, get-started, sign-in)
body:
## What

Restores the richer public experience the OAP-era stagecraft web app carried, ported onto the static apex and re-authored to be checkable against the real product family. Governed by the new **spec 004** (`specs/004-marketing-surfaces/spec.md`).

New surfaces:
- **Products / architecture** (`/products`): the family as layers (governance toolchain, substrate, control plane, interface, verification primitives), a governed delivery flow whose maturity chips roll up from the baked registry, and a repo catalog derived from the spec-003 roster so it cannot drift.
- **Papers + whitepaper reader** (`/papers`, `/papers/:slug`): sticky TOC, reading-progress, scroll-spy, inline `[ref:N]` references, a positioning table, and an interactive clickable-SVG architecture explorer. The flagship paper is re-authored around spec-spine, enrahitu, the attestation primitives (attest-ledger, tenant-emit, tenant-tail, canonical-keysort-json), action-gate/trust-window, and live Rauthy.
- **Get started** (`/get-started`): an honest split between what runs today (spec-spine, the enrahitu substrate) and what is on the ladder, each step linking to its governing spec.
- **Chrome**: Products, Papers, Get Started in the nav, plus a **Sign in** link.

## Honesty

Per this repo's rule (spec 002 section 1, CLAUDE.md), every published claim is checkable or marked forward-looking. No fabricated hashes, spec counts, signatures, OWASP "full coverage", or dead subsystems. The rename is total: "Open Agentic Platform"/"OAP" becomes Stagecraft; `factory-encore` and `template-encore` become `enrahitu`. Maturity is never hand-asserted where it could drift: the products delivery flow and the get-started/whitepaper framing are reconciled against the baked registry (Operate/fleet shows shipped because `stagecraft/006-fleet` is complete; the stamp and self-host steps link to genuinely in-progress specs).

## Sign-in

The static apex runs no auth flow. Sign in is a plain outbound link to `https://app.stagecraft.ing/auth/rauthy`: the same `/auth/rauthy` OIDC kickoff path the app used before the apex cutover, now on the control-plane host.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Pre-merge infra dependency: `app.stagecraft.ing` currently serves a self-signed K8s ingress cert and `/auth/rauthy` 404s (the control-plane deploy, `stagecraft/009-control-plane-deploy`, is in progress). Until that host has a valid cert and a landing/status page, clicking Sign in yields a browser TLS interstitial rather than a graceful hand-off. `auth.stagecraft.ing` (the Rauthy signer cited in the copy) is live with a valid cert.

## Static / deps

Icons are inline SVG (no new dependency); every new route is prerendered; the built output makes zero runtime off-origin requests.

## Gates

- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npm run build`: prerenders `/products`, `/papers`, `/papers/stagecraft-ecosystem`, `/get-started` and all existing routes
- `spec-spine compile` / `index` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check`: green
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main`: 17 paths checked, no drift, no waiver
- Independent review pass applied (fixed one status-contradiction, added keyboard activation to the explorer nodes)

Not merging: main auto-deploys to the live apex, so this awaits explicit approval.

title: docs(002): defer the product-family roster to spec 003
body:
## What

Trim spec 002 §2's "Product family table" bullet so it stops re-listing the ten repos inline and instead defers the roster **data** to its owner, spec 003 §3.

- **Kept in 002** (presentation contract): the index renders the family as a list; each row is a one-line role + repo link + SPDX license; stamped apps belong to their owners; the family list is broader than the `/registry` bake set (spec 001 §3).
- **Deferred to 003 §3** (the data): which repos, their roles, their licenses, encoded once in `app/lib/product-family.ts`.
- Also drops the stale "four repos" phrasing from the frontmatter `summary` (it is ten now, and a roster count does not belong in 002 anymore).

## Why

Spec 003 already declared itself the single owner of the roster (`app/lib/product-family.ts`). Leaving the full enumeration duplicated in 002 §2 was the last place the roster was restated outside its owner: a source of future drift. After this trim, 002 owns presentation, 003 owns data, 001 owns the `/registry` viewer, with no overlap.

## Governance

- Spec-only change. `spec-spine couple --base origin/main`: **OK, 0 paths checked, no drift** (no code touched, no `Spec-Drift-Waiver:` needed).
- Gates green: `compile` (4 specs, 0 warn), `index`, `lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0/0), `index check` (fresh).
- Regenerated `.derived/` shards for 002 included.

title: feat(003): product-family registry owns the shared repo list
body:
## Summary

`app/lib/product-family.ts` (the canonical product-family roster consumed by
the index page, the footer, and the `/registry` viewer's `repoMeta` lookup)
had no explicit spec owner: it fell under spec 001's `app/` directory while its
content was authored in spec 002 section 2. Every roster edit therefore tripped
the coupling gate and was cleared with a `Spec-Drift-Waiver:` (PR #2 added six
repos, PR #3 fixed the derived count).

Spec 003 gives the module a single explicit owner and carries the roster in its
section 3, so adding, removing, or re-describing a repo is an ordinary authoring
edit to spec 003 plus the module: it couples clean with no waiver and no edit to
the scaffold (001) or launch-content (002) specs. Marked `origin.retroactive:
true` because the module already exists (it shipped in PR #2); this spec adopts
it rather than claiming creation. No code change ships; the module already
matches the roster.

## Testing

- `spec-spine compile` (4 specs, 0 warnings), `index`, `lint --fail-on-warn`
  (0/0/0), `index check` (fresh).
- `spec-spine couple --base origin/main --head HEAD`: `OK, no drift` (this PR is
  spec-only, so no waiver is needed).
- Coupling-fix proof (throwaway temp branch, discarded): with
  `product-family.ts` changed and spec 003 in the range, `couple` reports

title: feat(002): expand the product family (tenant tools + 4 OAP primitives)
body:
## Summary

Expands the Stagecraft product family shown on the site from four repos to ten. All additions are public Apache-2.0 repos under stagecraft-ing, named and linked in the family list but NOT added to the /registry bake set (exactly like spec-spine), so the baked registry payload is unchanged.

Vended tenant tools:
- tenant-emit: signs a produced app's governance certificate.
- tenant-tail: re-verifies the factory's run-side paperwork with no trust in the producer.

OAP-extracted primitives:
- action-gate: a pure, deterministic decision gate (Allow / Deny / Degrade).
- attest-ledger: a tamper-evident, hash-linked, Ed25519-signed record ledger with an independent verifier.
- canonical-keysort-json: deterministic canonical JSON at the hash boundary.
- trust-window: a rolling-window trust scorer with graduated privilege output.

They join the footer product-family list, the README ecosystem list, and REPO_META/PRODUCT_FAMILY in app/lib/product-family.ts. Spec 002 section 2 records the expanded family (dated 2026-07-15). Also included: a small chore commit dropping blanket Write(**) from the .claude/settings.json allow list (the repo owner's own change).

## Testing

- spec-spine compile / index / lint --fail-on-warn / index check: all green.
- npm run typecheck: clean.
- npm run build: clean; the prerendered footer renders all 10 family repos; the baked payload's repo set stays the original four (enrahitu, stagecraft, stagecraft-cli, stagecraft.ing) and none of the new repos are baked as corpora.
- Roles and licenses are checkable against each repo's README, LICENSE, and GitHub description.

## Coupling

Spec-Drift-Waiver: app/lib/product-family.ts is spec-001-owned by directory (app/); the authoring edit for this family-list change lives in the content owner, spec 002 section 2. Spec 001 (scaffold) is intentionally not re-authored, per .claude/rules/adversarial-prompt-refusal.md.

title: feat(002): launch content, docs stubs, registry-derived status ladder
body:
## Spec 002: launch content

Implements `002-launch-content` end to end: the real index copy and the docs seed, replacing the spec-001 placeholders. No new build toolchain.

### What's here
- **Index** (`app/routes/_index.tsx`): hero, the Specify / Stamp / Operate / Verify loop, the product-family list, a for-agents block, and a live-registry pointer. Every capability claim carries a maturity chip and a receipt link resolved at build time from the spec that governs it, so the copy cannot read louder than the source.
- **Status ladder, M1 to M5** (`app/lib/milestones.ts`): rolled up from the baked registry, never hardcoded. At build time: **M1 shipped** (the EnRaHiTu chassis, `enrahitu/001` to `008`), **M2 in progress** (the template contract; the born-with certificate is still pending, so it is not claimed proven), **M3 to M5 planned**. The build fails loud if any referenced spec id stops resolving.
- **Docs** (`app/routes/docs.tsx` + `app/routes/docs.$slug.tsx` + `app/lib/docs.ts`): an index over three stubs (What is EnRaHiTu, The template contract, Self-hosting the control plane), each summarizing and linking its source, with an honest maturity marker.
- Spec 002 `establishes` corrected (Astro-era `src/content/` to the real `app/` paths) and marked complete; derived shards regenerated.

### Verification
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` clean; every route prerenders (including the three new docs pages); zero off-origin resource loads in the built output.
- Spine gates green locally: `compile`, `index check`, `lint --fail-on-warn`, and `couple` (with the waiver below).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: app/routes.ts and react-router.config.ts are spec-001 scaffold files, edited here only to register and prerender spec 002's new docs stub route (app/routes/docs.$slug.tsx). The changes are route wiring driven entirely by spec 002; spec 001's scaffold design is unchanged, so the complete spec 001 is not re-authored (per .claude/rules/adversarial-prompt-refusal.md).
